sections.body:
A bedroom is the room where you sleep and keep your things. It is your own space in the house.

Every bedroom has the same big parts. There is a **bed** for sleeping. There is a place to keep clothes, usually a **wardrobe**. There is a **shelf** or a desk for your books. And there is a floor for playing and reading.

A small bedroom in a house in Vietnam might have a wooden bed, a plastic wardrobe, a small desk and a mat on the floor. A bigger room might have a bookshelf, a chair and a rug.

The bed is the most important thing. You spend about a third of your life in bed. Good sleep helps you grow, helps you remember, and helps you feel calm in the morning.

Your bedroom shows who you are. The books on the shelf say what you like to read. The things on the wall say what you like to look at. Keeping it tidy makes it a happy place to be.
examples: This is my bedroom, where I sleep.
My books are on the shelf.
My clothes are in the wardrobe.
sections.heading: What a bedroom is, and why you need your own

sections.body:
A bed has a **mattress**. That is the soft part you lie on. Under the mattress there is a **bed base**, the strong frame that holds it up.

On the bed there is a **pillow**. You put your head on it. A **blanket** covers you when it is cold. A **sheet** is the thin cloth that goes on the mattress first.

At the end of the bed there may be a **headboard**. It is the tall board that stops you falling out of bed.

Beside the bed there may be a **nightstand**, a small table with a lamp on it. A **lamp** gives soft light so you can read at night. Some people keep a book and a glass of water there.

If you share a room with a brother or sister, you each have your own bed. You can hang a curtain to make your own little space.
examples: My head rests on the pillow.
I put a blanket on the bed because it is cold.
The lamp is on the nightstand.
sections.heading: The bed and the things around it

sections.body:
Every bedroom has things that are only for fun and things that are for learning.

Toys are the things you play with. Soft toys, toy cars, dolls and building blocks live in a **toy box** or a basket. Put them all back in the box when you finish, and the floor stays free to walk on.

Books are for reading. A **bookshelf** holds them upright. The tallest books often lean, so they do not fall over. Some children have a **book bag** for books they borrow from the school library.

Posters and pictures go on the wall. Use a piece of tape, not a nail, so the wall stays unbroken.

Some bedrooms have a **desk** with a chair. The desk is for writing and drawing, and the lamp on it helps your eyes in the evening.

And some bedrooms have a **trunk** or a **box** under the bed. That is where special things live, like a blanket you only use in winter.
examples: The building blocks go back in the toy box.
I keep my storybooks on the bookshelf.
I put a poster on the wall with some tape.
sections.heading: Toys, books and the things you keep

sections.body:
These are the words for the things in a bedroom. Once you know them, you can find anything you need.

A **pillow** is the soft thing under your head when you sleep.

A **blanket** is a thick warm cloth that covers you in bed.

A **wardrobe** is a tall cupboard where you hang your clothes.

A **shelf** is a flat board on the wall where you keep books or other things.

An **alarm clock** is a small clock that wakes you up in the morning.

Say these words out loud as you walk around your room. Point to each thing as you say it, and the words will stick.
examples: My head is on the pillow.
The blanket is on the bed.
Where is the alarm clock? It is on the shelf.
sections.heading: The bedroom words, one by one

terms.example: My pillow is soft and white.
terms.gloss: The soft thing under your head when you sleep in bed.

terms.example: I pull the blanket up to my chin.
terms.gloss: A thick warm cloth that covers you on cold nights.

terms.example: My school uniform hangs in the wardrobe.
terms.gloss: A tall cupboard with a door. You hang your clothes inside it.

terms.example: There are six books on the shelf.
terms.gloss: A flat board on the wall where you keep books and other things.

terms.example: My alarm clock rings at six.
terms.gloss: A small clock that rings in the morning to wake you up.

sections.body:
A tidy room is easy to keep tidy. Do these jobs in the same order every morning.

First, make the bed. Pull the blanket flat. Put the pillow at the head of the bed. Straighten the sheet.

Next, put the clothes away. Hang the shirts on hangers in the wardrobe. Fold the trousers and put them on the shelf.

Then, put the toys back. Everything in the toy box, and the lid on.

After that, check the desk. Put the pencils in the cup. Close the notebook. Put the books back where they belong.

Finally, open the window and let the fresh air in. A room with fresh air and a clear floor feels good to be in.

If your room is very big, clean one corner a day. Small jobs every day beat one big job at the weekend.
examples: I make my bed before breakfast.
The shirts go on the hangers.
I open the window to let the fresh air in.
sections.heading: How to make your room tidy
steps: Pull the blanket flat and straighten the pillow.
Hang the clothes in the wardrobe and fold the rest.
Put all the toys back in the toy box.
Put the pencils away and close the notebook.
Open the window to let the fresh air in.

sections.body:
You can make your room nice with very little. Try these ideas.

Keep one shelf just for your favourites. A photo, a small shell, a ticket from a show. These things make the room yours.

Use colours you like. A yellow wall feels warm. A blue curtain feels cool. A bright cushion makes a plain chair fun.

Let the daylight in during the day, and use a warm lamp in the evening. Your eyes feel better in the right light.

Keep the floor clear. You can walk around your room and play on the mat without tripping.

And look after your room at night. Keep a small light on, or plug in a night light, so you can find the door in the dark. Ask an adult to put a night light in the socket for you.
examples: My favourite shell is on the top shelf.
I keep my floor clear so I can play there.
The night light helps me find the door.
sections.heading: Making your room a happy place

item.summary: Your bedroom is your own little world. After reading this, you can name the things in a bedroom, say what each one is for, and keep your room clean and happy on your own.
item.title: What's Inside My Bedroom?
